questions.question: Who should receive a copy of comments on the draft Rifaximin Tablets monograph, in addition to the general IPC laboratory email address?
questions.answer: A copy of comments should be sent to Dr. Gaurav Pratap Singh (gpsingh.ipc@gov.in), alongside lab.ipc@gov.in.

questions.question: When was the first draft of the Rifaximin Tablets monograph posted on the IPC website for public comments?
questions.answer: The first draft was published on the IPC website for public comments on 28 November, 2022.

questions.question: How much sodium lauryl sulphate is added to the dissolution medium for Rifaximin Tablets of 400 mg and above?
questions.answer: For 400 mg and above strengths, 8 g of sodium lauryl sulphate is added to 1000 ml of the pH 7.4 phosphate buffer.

questions.question: What column temperature and detection wavelength are specified for the related substances LC test in the draft IP monograph for Rifaximin Tablets?
questions.answer: The column is held at 40º and the spectrophotometer is set at 276 nm.

questions.question: In the related substances test for Rifaximin Tablets, what is the minimum resolution required between the impurity D+H peaks and rifaximin for the test to be valid?
questions.answer: The resolution between the peaks due to impurity D+H and rifaximin must be not less than 3.0, otherwise the test is not valid.

questions.question: What is the concentration of the rifaximin IPRS reference solution used in the assay of Rifaximin Tablets in the draft IP monograph?
questions.answer: The reference solution is a 0.004 per cent w/v solution of rifaximin IPRS in the mobile phase.
